_comment: Reference solution for the layered-feature fixture. Not the only correct answer — merging layers 3 and 4, or splitting layer 2's store and auth apart, are both defensible. It exists so grade.sh can be sanity-checked against a known-good plan, and so the shape of a good plan is documented by example.

layers.title: Add users and sessions tables
layers.body:
## Stack position

**1 schema (this PR)** → 2 store → 3 api → 4 ui

Review bottom-up; this is the bottom.

## What this layer does

Adds the `users` and `sessions` tables plus the forward/back migration.

## Intentionally missing

No callers yet — the session store that reads these tables lands in layer 2 (`auth/2-store`). Nothing in this PR references the new tables, which is expected for a schema-only foundation layer.

layers.title: Add session store and token verification
layers.body:
## Stack position

1 schema → **2 store (this PR)** → 3 api → 4 ui

Depends on layer 1 for the `sessions` table.

## What this layer does

Adds the session read/write path against the schema from layer 1, and replaces `LegacyVerify` with `Verify`. The rename of `legacy_token.go` → `token.go` is in this layer along with every call site, so no layer is left referencing a deleted file.

## Intentionally missing

The HTTP surface that calls into this store lands in layer 3.

layers.title: Add auth endpoints
layers.body:
## Stack position

1 schema → 2 store → **3 api (this PR)** → 4 ui

Depends on layers 1 and 2.

## What this layer does

Adds the auth HTTP handlers on top of the session store from layer 2.

## Intentionally missing

No UI yet — the sign-in form lands in layer 4. The only callers here are within the package (layer-boundary self-containment exception).

layers.title: Add sign-in UI and integration tests
layers.body:
## Stack position

1 schema → 2 store → 3 api → **4 ui (this PR)** ← top

Depends on layers 1-3.

## What this layer does

Adds the sign-in UI that calls the layer-3 endpoints, plus the integration tests that exercise the whole flow. Carries the regenerated `package-lock.json`, which is excluded from the review budget and rides along rather than justifying a layer of its own.

## Full change

Compare `auth/4-ui` against `main` for the complete feature.
